result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the concrete problem behaviours and propose good fixes for defaults, grouping and saving. B goes further on recoverability: it adds undo toasts, a settings snapshot before reset, in-place sync-failure status and a per-hive reset, and it is more careful in its claims ('can't confirm without the review text'). A has stronger post-release instrumentation but overclaims that the setting order is 'almost certainly the main cause', so B edges it overall. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers name all four problem behaviours, propose sensible default-on alerts with copy-from-hive, switch to save-as-you-go, drop the unit confirmation and move the reset, and group the 38 settings without removing any. A is stronger on recoverability: it adds undo toasts and a settings snapshot so the reset can be undone, and it is careful about thresholds converting correctly when the unit changes. B is stronger on what to watch after release, with instrumentation, a tally of reviews and tickets, and a staged rollout, but it overstates when it calls the ordering 'almost certainly' the main cause.
